chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman from 'Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Talhah ibn Zayd from Abu 'Abdillah from his father, upon them be peace:

That a man gave a house of his as charity while he was living in it, so the Imam said to him, 'Leave it now.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is based on a type of recommendation (istihbab), because we have clarified in the narration of Abu al-Jaroud from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that it is permissible for a person to live in a house he has endowed (waqf) along with the person he endowed it for, and that this is not forbidden.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a donor to live in a house they have donated as charity?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal status of waqf (endowment) where the donor retains residence, resolving apparent contradictions by classifying the Imam's command to leave as recommended (istihbab) rather than obligatory. Shaykh al-Tusi highlights that this flexibility allows the donor to live in the endowed property, provided it aligns with the conditions set by the donee, reflecting the pragmatic application of Shia jurisprudence in charitable endowments.
